FROM THE OPENING UP

CGC / ground-up storefront installation film

An empty opening becomes a finished glass storefront through work you can see: set the sill, align the frame, seat the glass, finish the joint, fit the door. The final reveal is earned by those physical actions.

Creative line: Built from the opening up.

This is a new alternate concept for Commercial Glazing Contractors Inc., not a rendered video or a record of an actual CGC project. It covers installation of a storefront into an existing commercial building shell. It does not depict CGC constructing the building or pouring its foundations. The approximate opening dimensions below are fictional scene-design dimensions, not claims about a CGC job.

Film structure

Eight shots. Twenty-four seconds. Silent website master at 24fps, 576 frames. Also export a sound-design version for presentation if wanted. White stucco, graphite aluminum, clear glass and restrained steel-blue reflections. Bright neutral daylight throughout. The excitement comes from material, weight, alignment and the change in the opening, not flash transitions.

The storyboard reads left to right, top to bottom. It is a visual direction sheet, not a set of production-ready keyframes. Panel 02 includes an upright jamb although the shot should isolate the sill before upright framing; correct this in its clean start frame. Panel 05 is illustrative of handling but needs a clearly visible gap above the sill before seating. Panel 07 needs a visible gap between the supported door leaf and its jamb. Do not animate the storyboard collage, panel numbers or these ambiguous poses.

Lock the storefront before generating

Use the overall architecture of panel 08 as the visual direction. Make a clean straight-on final elevation first. Opening approximately 24 feet wide by 10 feet high; white stucco piers at both sides; flat graphite fascia above; pale concrete sidewalk; same unfinished retail interior behind it. Fix one horizontal transom, two fixed-glass bays at left and one narrower single-door bay at right. Choose and record exact normalized mullion positions in the final elevation, then hold them for every stage. No second door, additional window or changing transom height.

Create three aligned wide continuity plates with the same lens, tripod position and architecture: empty opening, complete frame with empty pockets, completed glazing with door closed. Derive stages from the same reference. Do not independently invent eight buildings from text. The generated board has small geometry differences and is not the geometry authority.

Use a flat-on 35mm-equivalent wide view as the continuity anchor; close-ups are separately composed from that geometry. Daylight comes from upper left, the sidewalk and roof remain fixed, and exterior reflections must match the surrounding scene. No logos, readable signs, client branding or invented address. No change to sunset, trees or occupied showroom between stages.

Workers: two adult installers in plain charcoal/gray workwear, hard hats, eye protection and gloves. Keep wardrobe and number consistent. Avoid face close-ups. Hands hold tools or handles with stable contact. Glass lites remain rigid rectangles with plausible thickness and edges. Support and handling must look credible; do not use precarious overhead loads or workers under suspended glass. This is cinematic direction, not a field installation procedure. Have a glazing professional review the depicted details before publishing them as representative work.

Production assignment for Freebuff

Produce actual generated clips, inspect them, and assemble this exact sequence if this concept is selected. Do not return a revised brief as if the movie were delivered. This alternate package does not automatically replace Threshold v4 or In Plain Sight; preserve the current hero until the owner selects a film and the new exports pass inspection. Keep the work focused on the film; website audits are not a substitute for production.

Start with the installed Wan2GP MiniMax H3 FL2VA Pruned preset. Verify that its weights, image conditioning, resolution, duration and memory/offload settings actually work on the local machine. The installed model is a starting candidate, not a claim that it can perform these actions correctly. Use clean start/end images where the actual preset supports them. End conditioning may guide a physical move; it must not be used to excuse a dissolve or shape morph between two states.

Qualification is mandatory before the full batch: I05 glass seating and I07 door alignment. They test hand-object contact, rigidity, support and real installation motion. Make one faithful attempt and up to two focused revisions per qualification shot. Keep the prescribed action and camera. If H3 fails, test another already-installed suitable image-to-video model on the same shot. Do not download weights, add credentials or silently change workflows. Record the preset, model files, settings, seed, source images and result for every attempt.

If no tested local model can produce either installation action correctly, stop with the failing clips and a precise blocker. Do not finish the film with fake still movement, omit the hard shots or claim that an alternative action matches. Request approval before a live-action or other production substitution. No artificial progress claims while a render has not completed.

Generate enough source frames for each edit duration, with handles where practical. A model duration limit means render a longer valid source or split into approved source takes preserving the required operation. Never hold the last frame, interpolate a still into a camera move, reverse a removal clip, or use lens zoom to fill time. Trim to the exact boundaries below. The first and last frames differ; use a deliberate hard cut on website replay, not a promise of a seamless loop.

Global acceptance gates

A locked-camera shot has no intentional pan, truck, dolly or zoom. Only the prescribed worker/object action moves. Reject camera movement even if the clip looks attractive.

I01 requires a real rightward truck. I08 requires a real pullback. Near and far geometry must move differently through parallax. Digital scale, an animated crop or a held image fails.

Panels do not grow, bend, liquefy, merge into hands, change tint or pass through metal. Aluminum members do not appear out of nowhere.

Each installation action starts visibly incomplete, progresses physically and ends visibly closer to the intended installed state. A stationary installer pose with flickering hands fails.

Cuts may omit elapsed work between operations. Individual clips must not transform the whole facade to jump between construction stages.

Keep the same opening, mullion layout, door side, light direction and crew. Reject a handsome shot of a different storefront.

All eight shots must pass their individual action and geometry checks. A mean quality score cannot hide a failed mandatory action.

For every attempt extract first, 25%, 50%, 75% and last frames plus a contact sheet. Watch the complete clip at normal speed and half speed. Check rigid edges, hand contact, camera direction, glass/frame clearance, continuity and end state. Frame samples alone cannot prove correct movement. If available, use point tracks or optical flow as supporting evidence; visual inspection of the clip remains required. Record pass/fail reasons, not just adjectives such as cinematic.

Eight shot cards

I01 / The opening

00–02s / frames 0–47 / 48 edited frames

Start state

White stucco shell with completely empty rough opening; no sill receiver, aluminum members, glass or door.

Required physical action

Camera trucks right by a short distance at fixed height and orientation. Near white pier drifts left more than the back wall. No construction action in this establishing shot.

End state

Same empty opening seen slightly farther from the right. Opening dimensions, unfinished interior and daylight unchanged.

Camera

35mm-equivalent medium-wide. True rightward truck, fixed lens and level orientation. Do not pan to keep the opening centered.

Clean start-frame prompt

Clean photorealistic 16:9 exterior medium-wide frame of the continuity storefront before any glazing work. Empty rectangular opening in white stucco, graphite fascia, pale concrete sidewalk, unfinished interior. Match the approved clean final elevation in building dimensions and position, but remove all glazing-system components. Camera just left of center, daylight upper left. No people, lettering, overlays or panel numbers.

H3 motion prompt

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] The camera translates smoothly to the right beside the empty storefront opening. The nearby white pier moves left faster than the unfinished interior back wall, creating real depth parallax. Building remains fixed and opening remains entirely empty. Fixed lens, level camera. No framing or glass appears.
overall_soundscape: Quiet site ambience. No speech.
non_diegetic_music: None.

Reject if

Push-in, lens zoom, pan, digital scale, still plate, spontaneous construction, changing shell.

Recovery: preserve the action

Shorten the rightward travel and use a closer pier for visible depth. Retain the truck; never replace it with a push.

I02 / Set the base

02–05s / frames 48–119 / 72 edited frames

Start state

Close view of the lower opening. A short visible portion of graphite sill receiver is supported just above its intended substrate position by gloved hands. No upright jamb already installed in this shot.

Required physical action

Hands lower the rigid receiver a small distance and bring it to rest in its prepared position. One small physical placement only; do not attempt the entire sill assembly in one clip.

End state

Receiver rests stationary against its intended base position, hands still supporting it. No assertion that anchorage or weatherproofing has been completed.

Camera

Tripod-locked close detail, low oblique angle, receiver and substrate in same plane of focus. Zero camera movement.

Clean start-frame prompt

Photorealistic low close-up of the base of the same white-stucco storefront opening before uprights or glass. Two work-gloved hands support a straight graphite sill receiver a small visible distance above its prepared base. Receiver and substrate gap both readable. Match pale concrete and upper-left daylight. No upright jamb, labels or numbers. Clean 16:9.

I05 / Seat the glass

10–14s / frames 240–335 / 96 edited frames

Start state

One fixed bay is shown close enough to read its lower pocket. Two installers support a rigid upright clear-glass lite on suction handles; lower edge visibly a small distance above its intended supported seat. Top is already aligned for this small final seating move. Adjacent bays may remain empty.

Required physical action

Both installers guide the supported lite down through the short remaining distance into its prepared seat. Glass must move relative to the fixed frame. Stop with support still maintained; no suction release required.

End state

Bottom edge is visibly seated, pane remains upright and supported, frame and lite dimensions unchanged. Do not depict unseen fastening or claim the whole bay is finished.

Camera

Absolutely locked medium close view. Include lower gap, rigid glass edge, fixed frame and both suction contact points. No camera motion.

Clean start-frame prompt

Photorealistic medium close view of a fixed bay in the same graphite frame. Two consistent installers support one transparent rigid rectangular glass lite with suction handles. Show its lower edge visibly a few centimeters above the prepared lower seat, with plausible clearance and top alignment. Hands on handles, glass edge unobscured. No floating glass, unsafe load or text.

H3 motion prompt

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Locked camera. The two installers keep both suction handles attached and lower the single rigid glass lite slowly through the short visible remaining gap into its prepared lower seat. The bottom glass edge descends relative to the stationary aluminum sill until contact is visible. The pane remains rectangular, clear, upright and supported. All other frame members stay fixed. No glass bending, dissolve, growth or camera move.
overall_soundscape: Quiet site ambience. No speech.
non_diegetic_music: None.

Reject if

No relative pane/frame displacement; panel fades in; pane bends or passes through metal; handles detach; hands slide through glass; base gap concealed; zoom or moving camera.

I06 / Finish the joint

14–17s / frames 336–407 / 72 edited frames

Start state

Fixed lite already installed. Macro view of a short unfinished straight perimeter joint; nozzle positioned at its starting end. Other installation and retention operations happened between cuts.

Required physical action

A gloved hand moves the nozzle left to right, laying one short continuous bead only where the nozzle has passed. The bead grows from contact with the nozzle, not by an independent animated line.

End state

One short neat bead remains behind the nozzle. Existing glass and aluminum stay fixed.

Camera

Tripod-locked macro with a shallow but readable focus plane along the joint. No sweep, push or zoom.

Clean start-frame prompt

Clean photorealistic macro of a straight perimeter joint between installed clear glass and graphite aluminum on the same storefront. A gloved hand holds a sealant applicator nozzle at the left start of a short unfilled joint. Nozzle contact and remaining joint visible. Fine material texture, no words or diagrams.

H3 motion prompt

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Locked macro camera. A gloved hand guides the applicator nozzle steadily from left to right along the short fixed glass-to-aluminum joint. One continuous small sealant bead remains immediately behind the moving nozzle. The glass and frame do not move, and the bead appears only where the nozzle has passed. No floating luminous line or camera movement.
overall_soundscape: Quiet site ambience. No speech.
non_diegetic_music: None.

Reject if

Bead appears ahead of nozzle, nozzle floats, joint moves, tools melt, wrong travel direction, camera sweep.

Recovery: preserve the action

Use a shorter straight joint and slower hand travel. Keep nozzle contact readable. Rerender instead of adding a graphic line.

End state

Complete finished storefront is readable as a whole. Same white piers, two fixed bays, transom and right-side single door. No change of time or location.

Camera

Edit, sound and phone version

Hard cuts connect work stages; no morph transitions, bright flashes or speed ramps concealing errors. Match the frame's verticals and screen position through the first four stages. Use the glass lowering motion to cut into the perimeter finish, then the door operation, then a clean reveal. The final wide holds only as part of a continuously moving pullback.

Optional sound: restrained site air, sill contact, short metal contact, suction-handle handling, a dry tool movement and a quiet final door latch recorded or licensed appropriately. Avoid generic hammering over every shot. No dialogue or model-generated music. The silent website master must make the sequence understandable without sound. Optional on-page text should be real HTML, not burned into model output: Rough opening / Aluminum frame / Glass set / Finished entrance.

Create a separately considered 9:16 version. A center crop from 16:9 retains only about 31.6% of its width. Keep hands, supported panel, lower pocket and required end state visible together. If the action does not fit, create a dedicated portrait source take with the same action and geometry. Do not crop away a missing installation step and call it acceptable. Keep the right-side door visible in the final portrait composition.
